## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide AOT kernel for integration+decide that emits a 1 B/p mask, paired with a host-side respawn scan, can decouple vectorizable math from branchy control flow and approach the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The AoS Particle at 69 B/p offers poor locality: loops 1 and 3 touch 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot), loop 2 touches 4 of 68 B/p (5% hot); the mask intermediate adds 1 B/p. The approach calls `halide_b6_mask` (AOT) for math+decide, then a host-side mask scan drives respawn, then a scalar render pass. The 59% dead bytes in loops 1/3 and 95% in loop 2 waste most streamed bandwidth. The working set spills L1d at N≈474 and L2 at N≈7598, but codegen bloat prevents exploiting the smaller hot set.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p rises gently from 21.0 (L1d, N=320) to ~24.5 (L3, N=10000), stabilizing at 23-26 through DRAM. No knee marks the L1d→L2 or L2→L3 transitions — the algo is already 4x above the 5.437 ns/p floor and frontend-bound, so cache residency is irrelevant. The L3→DRAM spill at N≈250000 adds only ~1 ns/p (23.2→24.1). At higher death rates DRAM degrades more: q=0.25 jumps from 27.3 (N=160000) to 32.5 (N=370000), a 19% step, as the branchy respawn fires over DRAM-resident particles.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 2.0-3.3 GB/s against the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 16-26% — and 4-6x above the 5.437 ns/p floor. The verdict is frontend-bound: at N=10000, q=0.01, frontend_stall is 67.0%, backend 0.1%, branch_flush 0.0%. The algo matches naive scalar (0.95x baseline at q=0.01, N=320) and is 2.84x slower than the winner. At q=0.5 it edges ahead of naive (0.85x baseline at N=320) but remains 1.70x slower than the winner. At DRAM, q=0.1 pushes backend_stall to 16.7% and compute drops to 12.5%.

## Assembly
The codegen is overwhelmingly scalar: 14 of 629 instructions are vector-suffixed. The render loop runs ~484 insns/iter with 98 conditional branches, scalar FP (`vmovss`, `vmulss`, `vaddss`, `vsubss`, `vucomiss`, `vcvttss2si`), and 17 byte-granular scatter stores (`movzx`+`mov BYTE PTR`). The respawn scan is 32-way unrolled: `vmovdqu`+`vptest` skip all-zero chunks, but each live byte triggers `cmp BYTE PTR`→`je`→`call spawn` with `vzeroupper` (34 total). This footprint exceeds the µop cache, explaining the 67% frontend stall. The cmov chain (×12) cannot compensate for byte-granular writes that prevent streaming.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01, N=320 the algo runs 0.95x baseline and 2.84x slower than the winner; at q=0.5, N=320 it is 0.85x baseline but still 1.70x slower than the winner; at N=10000000, q=0.01 it is 1.024x baseline and 2.49x slower than the winner. The Halide AOT kernel generates the mask, but the host-side respawn scan — 32-way unrolled byte comparisons with per-particle `call spawn`, 98 branches/iter, and 17 byte-granular scatter stores — creates a 67% frontend stall no cache regime or death rate overcomes.
